newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat says will set up state despite Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says will set up state despite Israel.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Wednesday that he would eventually declare a Palestinian state despite opposition from Israel.

"The Palestinian state is not an Israeli issue. This is an Arab and international issue. After the interim agreements, we will declare an independent Palestinian state," Arafat told reporters at the Arab League.
The Palestinian leader flew into Cairo from Italy and held talks with both Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel Meguid.

He was responding to remarks made on Monday by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in which he said the Jewish state would respond severely if Arafat declared a Palestinian state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Israel on Friday transferred control of most of the West Bank town of Hebron to Arafat's Palestinian Authority. The authority now controls the Gaza Strip and eight West Bank towns handed over by Israel under several agreements signed since 1993.
The final status of these areas, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war, is to be determined in negotiations ending no later than May 1999.
Arafat views Palestinian statehood as the natural culmination of these negotiations while Netanyahu rejects the establishment of a Palestinian state, saying statehood could endanger Israel.

Both sides also disagree about the final status of Arab East Jerusalem, which Israel also captured in the 1967 war. Netanyahu has repeated the Israeli line that an undivided Jerusalem is the eternal capital of the Jewish state. The Palestinians say they want the eastern part as the capital of their future state.

"Netanyahu should not forget that Jerusalem is part of the lands that Israel occupied in the war and that he was there at the Madrid conference when we agreed on the land-for-peace principle...Jerusalem is part of that," Arafat told reporters.
Egypt, which regards itself as an unofficial sponsor of the Middle East peace talks that started with the 1991 Madrid conference, has sided with the Palestinians on the issue of Jerusalem.
Before leaving for Gaza, Arafat told reporters at Cairo airport that he was soliciting Egyptian support for the next stage of Israeli-Palestinian talks.
